verdict.summary: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio, so you must register your own app in the bexio Developer Portal and paste its client ID and secret into Composio. Registration itself is quick and no review is documented for OAuth apps, but the redirect URI must match exactly, the scope list is fixed at consent, and public listing in the marketplace has real partner thresholds.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 45-90 min for registration and first connection; more if you pursue marketplace listing
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1 hour, including account setup if you do not already have a bexio account
verdict.approval_wait: None documented for creating an OAuth app; no public review timeline was found (unverified)

gates.name: Own app, own bexio account
gates.unlocks: Create the app in the Developer Portal and connect your own bexio account through Composio.
limits: Account must have administrator permissions (community guide).
Free 30-day trial is enough to own the app.
Developer Portal terms must be accepted.

gates.name: No separate invited-user tier documented
gates.unlocks: Not documented. The findings show no test-user allowlist, development store, or install cap for bexio OAuth apps, so treat other bexio customers as needing Gate 3 until confirmed.
limits: No published user count, install limit, or token-expiry cap for test users was found.
Refresh-token session closes if not renewed within 1 year (applies to all users).

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public distribution)
gates.unlocks: Listing in the bexio marketplace, which advertises 10,000 visitors per month. API access itself is not restricted by bexio.
limits: At least 10 bexio customers among regular clients.
At least 20 active users of the app.
App available in two of German, French, Italian, English; marketplace content in all four.
Marketplace partner agreement and partnership application form.
Must implement bexio API and OpenID Connect login and offer customer support.

steps.title: Create a bexio account
steps.detail: Sign up for a bexio account or start the free 30-day trial, which needs no installation or payment. Use an account with administrator permissions, since that account will own the app.
gotchas: A community guide says the account needs administrator permissions; the official pages do not confirm this.

steps.title: Log in to the Developer Portal
steps.detail: Open the Developer Portal and log in with your bexio credentials. The portal root is public and does not show a login wall, so you will only be prompted at login.

steps.title: Accept the Developer Portal terms
steps.detail: Read and accept the terms and conditions. Read Section 4.4 on commercial use before accepting, since it applies if you plan to charge customers or distribute the app.

steps.title: Create the app and set the redirect URL
steps.detail: Create a new app. In the "Allowed redirect URL" field, enter the exact Composio callback URL from your Composio auth config. You can register up to ten redirect URLs, for example one for test and one for production; the value must match exactly or sign-in fails.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs must be declared at registration; bexio does not accept arbitrary targets.
Any difference (scheme, trailing slash, host) causes sign-in to fail with an error.
Whether the portal accepts Composio's callback was not verified by a live registration.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the app and expand the "App Details" section to reveal the Client ID and Client Secret. Store the secret in your password manager or secret store.

values.label: Location
values.value: App Details section of the app in developer.bexio.com

gotchas: The app must be server-side because the token exchange sends the client secret. Do not put the secret in browser or mobile code.

steps.title: Choose the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Draft a scope list for the agent's actual use cases and a one-line justification per scope. Do not copy Composio's default list, which has about 39 scopes including payroll; users see every scope on the consent page and scopes cannot be added later without re-authorization. Write scopes grant read access automatically, so do not add separate read scopes.

values.label: Example business scopes
values.value: contact_show contact_edit kb_invoice_show kb_invoice_edit project_show note_show

gotchas: Payroll scopes are only needed for payroll endpoints; most apps do not need them.
The changelog of 2026-06-19 updated required scopes for purchase bill, payment and expense endpoints; check these if your app uses them.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create a bexio auth config that uses your own OAuth app (not the managed one, which is unavailable). Paste the Client ID and Client Secret, and set the scopes to the list from the previous step. Confirm the Composio callback URL matches the one in the portal.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's default scope list is very broad; override it with your minimum list.

steps.title: Verify the endpoints
steps.detail: Confirm the authorize and token URLs respond from the realm path. The root OpenID discovery URL returned 404, so do not rely on it; use the realm-scoped endpoints published in the docs.

steps.title: Connect your own account and check the consent screen
steps.detail: Start the connection in Composio and sign in with your bexio user. Read the consent page; it lists the permissions bexio will give the app. Your user must have bexio permissions for each area, since the API also checks the user's rights.

steps.title: Plan for scope changes and token refresh
steps.detail: Build the app so refresh requests keep the existing scopes and so any new scope triggers a full re-authorization. Store the refresh token and replace it with any new one returned on refresh. Treat a connection with no refresh for one year as expired.
gotchas: Refreshing never adds scopes; the user must sign in again for new ones.
Access token lifetime was not found in the docs.
Whether refresh tokens rotate was not confirmed.

steps.title: Handle user identity and rate limits
steps.detail: Use the sub claim only as an opaque user ID, since the current IdP issues it as a UUID. Keep the bexio company ID from the company_profile claim if you request that scope. Back off on HTTP 429 using the RateLimit headers; the numeric per-minute limit is not published.
gotchas: Older tokens from the decommissioned idp.bexio.com host may need migration.

steps.title: Confirm who can install the app before inviting others
steps.detail: The findings do not describe a test-user list or install cap for OAuth apps. Before inviting customers outside your own company, test with one second bexio account and confirm with bexio support that other companies can authorize your app.
gotchas: No public approval process for OAuth apps was found.

steps.title: Decide whether to apply for a marketplace listing
steps.detail: Skip this step if you only need your own company or a few clients. For public listing, check the thresholds: at least 10 bexio customers, at least 20 active users, two of the four languages, and a signed marketplace partner agreement. Then submit the partnership application form.
gotchas: The listing review timeline was not found.
Partners must offer customer support for the app.

steps.title: Wait for marketplace review, if you applied
steps.detail: If you submitted a listing application, bexio reviews it. No timeline or rejection reasons were published in the findings.

blockers.symptom: Sign-in fails with an error after authorization.
blockers.cause: Redirect URL does not exactly match the value registered on the app.
blockers.fix: Copy the Composio callback URL exactly into the Allowed redirect URL field and re-test.

blockers.symptom: Users see permissions they do not need, or the app cannot do a new action after launch.
blockers.cause: Scope list was too broad at registration; new scopes require a full re-authorization by each user.
blockers.fix: Request only needed scopes up front and plan a re-consent flow for future scope additions.

blockers.cause: Per-company rate limit per minute; the numeric limit is not published.
blockers.fix: Read RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset headers and back off.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace listing application is not accepted.
blockers.cause: Thresholds not met (10 customers, 20 active users, language coverage, partner agreement).
blockers.fix: Meet the thresholds before applying, or stay on direct installs without listing.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio. Start with your own app from the bexio Developer Portal and paste the client ID and secret into Composio. Override Composio's default scope list (about 39 scopes, including payroll) with the minimum you need, since consent shows every scope and new scopes need re-authorization.

evidence.claim: Composio reports no managed OAuth for bexio, so the developer must register their own app and bring a client ID and secret.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available": false
flags: no probe was run against this host

evidence.claim: The official setup begins with creating a bexio account (a trial account is sufficient) and then signing in to the Developer Portal with those credentials.
evidence.quote: Go to the developer portal at https://developer.bexio.com and log in using your bexio credentials.

evidence.claim: The developer must read and accept the Developer Portal terms, and section 4.4 on commercial use is singled out.
evidence.quote: Read and accept the terms and conditions (please pay special attention to the commercial use regulations mentioned in Section 4.4).

evidence.claim: After creating a new app in the portal, the developer must enter at least one valid allowed redirect URL.
evidence.quote: Create a new app and make sure that you define a valid site for the "Allowed redirect URL" field(s)

evidence.claim: The client ID and client secret are revealed under the App Details section of the app in the portal.
evidence.quote: By clicking on the section "App Details" you can reveal the Client ID and Client Secret

evidence.claim: Redirect URLs must be declared during app registration; bexio does not accept arbitrary redirect targets.
evidence.quote: The new bexio API platform requires to define redirect URLs during the app registration in the developer port

evidence.claim: Up to ten redirect addresses can be registered per app, which the community guide uses for test and production environments.
evidence.quote: Up to ten addresses are possible, for instance for test and production.

evidence.claim: The redirect URL must match the registered value exactly, otherwise sign-in fails.
evidence.quote: it has to match the Developer Portal exactly, otherwise sign-in stops with an error message.

evidence.claim: Web origins for browser-based (CORS) requests can be added by registering the origin as a redirect URL on the developer portal.
evidence.quote: These issues can be mitigated by adding your web origin as a valid redirect URL for your app on https://developer.bexio.com.

evidence.claim: The developer portal responds with HTTP 200 and no login wall at the root URL.
evidence.quote: "title": "bexio Developer Portal", "login_wall": false

evidence.claim: The authorize endpoint is live and rejects an unknown client ID with a 'client not found' error page rather than an OAuth error redirect.
evidence.quote: Something went wrong. Client nicht gefunden.

evidence.claim: The OpenID Connect endpoints are published in the docs: issuer, authorization, token, userinfo, and JWK endpoints under the realm path on auth.bexio.com.
evidence.quote: Authorization endpoint https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth

evidence.claim: A standard OIDC discovery document was not found at the domain root: the discovery probe got 404 at auth.bexio.com/.well-known/openid-configuration, while the docs point to a realm-scoped discovery URL instead.
The app must be server-side, because the token exchange sends the client secret and the secret must be kept safe.
evidence.quote: Your app must be server-side because during this exchange, you must also pass along your application's Client Secret

evidence.claim: Authentication uses the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant, with OpenID Connect layered on top; bexio documents a single flow.
evidence.quote: bexio supports the "Authorization Code Grant" as defined in OAuth 2.0 RFC 6749, section 4.1 to obtain an Access Token.

evidence.claim: Scopes are space-separated, and a write scope automatically grants read access to the same resource, so a separate read scope is not needed.
evidence.quote: Read access is granted automatically when a write scope is requested for a resource.

evidence.claim: bexio asks the developer to request only the scopes the app needs.
evidence.quote: Please only request the scopes that you need for your application.

evidence.claim: The OIDC scopes openid and offline_access are the ones that trigger an ID token and a refresh token; offline_access is required for refresh.
evidence.quote: The scope offline_access is required to obtain a refresh token to keep the api connection alive.

evidence.claim: Optional OIDC scopes add identity claims: profile, email, and company_profile (company_id, company_name) each add claims to the ID token or userinfo.
evidence.quote: Adds company specific claims to the id token like company_id and company_name

evidence.claim: Scopes are granted by the user who sets up the connection, and API access also depends on that user's bexio permissions; both must allow the call.
evidence.quote: The scopes are granted by the user who sets up the connection to the application.

evidence.claim: Refreshing a token does not change the granted scopes; new scopes need a full new authorization by the user.
evidence.quote: Acquiring new scopes is only possible by going through the initial authorization process again.

evidence.claim: The consent screen lists the requested permissions to the user before they grant access.
evidence.quote: The user authenticates and sees a consent page listing the permissions bexio will give to the web application.

evidence.claim: Representative scope list includes contact_show and contact_edit (contacts), kb_invoice_show and kb_invoice_edit (invoices), project_show, note_show, and payroll scopes; payroll ones are not required for most apps.
evidence.quote: kb_invoice_show Read access to invoices kb_invoice_edit Write access to invoices

evidence.claim: The docs state that payroll scopes were added to the scope section and that the scopes are required for payroll endpoints.
evidence.quote: Payroll scopes have been added to the API Scopes section

evidence.claim: Consent cannot be reused for new scopes: a connection that needs more rights must be re-authorized by the user.
evidence.quote: If the app needs more, the user has to sign in again.

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens need the offline_access scope; the offline session is closed if a refresh is not made within one year.
evidence.quote: The returned refresh token will be valid indefinitely but the associated offline session will be closed if not renewed within 1 year.

evidence.claim: Using the current identity provider, the user ID claim is sub, which is now a UUID rather than an email; login_id is the stable value to use.
evidence.quote: sub - This claim identifies the user who granted the creation of the token.

evidence.claim: Tokens and client configs may need migration if they came from the older IdP host, which has been decommissioned.
evidence.quote: idp.bexio.com will be decommissioned on 31.03.2025.

evidence.claim: The API enforces a per-company rate limit per minute; excess calls get HTTP 429, with RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining, and -Reset headers.
evidence.quote: The bexio API enforces a rate limit that limits the number of requests a company can make per minute.

evidence.claim: The numeric per-minute limit is not published; one third-party integration docs note it is not published.
evidence.quote: Currently, the limit is not published.

evidence.claim: bexio states that anyone can build an integration with its API; API access is not restricted.
evidence.quote: We do not restrict API access: anyone can develop an integration with bexio.

evidence.claim: A marketplace listing requires at least 10 bexio customers among regular clients.
evidence.quote: At least 10 bexio customers (SMEs or fiduciaries) among your regular clientele.

evidence.claim: A marketplace listing requires at least 20 active users of the app.
evidence.quote: At least 20 active users of your app.

evidence.claim: Marketplace partners must implement the bexio API and OpenID Connect login, and offer customer support for the app.
evidence.quote: Integration via bexio API and OpenID Connect login.

evidence.claim: The app must be available in two of German, French, Italian and English, with marketplace content in all four.
evidence.quote: app in two languages, marketplace content in all four.

evidence.claim: Marketplace partners sign a marketplace partner agreement, and interested developers submit a partnership application form.
evidence.quote: You sign the marketplace partner agreement.

evidence.claim: Listed partners reach an advertised audience of 10,000 marketplace visitors per month.
evidence.quote: present your solution to 10,000 visitors to our marketplace every month

evidence.claim: A community guide says the bexio account must have administrator permissions, but a free trial is enough for the developer side.
evidence.quote: A bexio account with administrator permissions: The account is only there to own the app you register.

evidence.claim: A bexio free trial is available with no installation or payment needed.
evidence.quote: Start a free 30-day trial with no obligation

evidence.claim: The API documentation published a changelog entry on 2026-06-19 updating required scopes for purchase bills, payment, and expense endpoints.
evidence.quote: 2026-06-19 Required scopes updated for purchase bills, payment and expense endpoints.

evidence.claim: The docs mention a Redocly-based API reference, status page, and developer newsletter, and that no guided implementation or code support is provided.
evidence.quote: there is no guided implementation or code support available.

evidence.claim: A cross-check: no published public review, approval, or verification timeline for OAuth apps was found in the bexio docs or the marketplace page.

open_questions: No public review, verification, or consent-approval process for OAuth apps (outside the marketplace) was found. Unknown whether bexio manually approves an app before customers outside the developer's own company can connect.
Whether the Developer Portal accepts Composio's callback URL (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add per the toolkit config) was not verified by a live registration.
Numeric per-minute rate limit and plan-tier dependence are not published; one third-party claim about plan tiers is unverified.
PKCE support on auth.bexio.com was not documented in the pages read.
Redirect URI matching rules beyond exact match (http vs https, localhost, wildcards) were not confirmed.
Access token lifetime was not found in the pages read.
Whether refresh tokens rotate on each refresh was not explicitly confirmed.
Privacy policy, homepage, logo, domain verification, and security assessment requirements for a developer app were not found; only marketplace requirements were listed.
Marketplace review timeline and rejection reasons were not found.
Developer Portal's exact account prerequisites (org admin vs. user) were not confirmed on an official page; the admin requirement comes from a community guide.
Whether the sub vs. login_id claim guidance is current was not confirmed from the cited pages.
Whether a Personal Access Token is a viable alternative for a single-company agent was not assessed; PATs are for personal scripts, not apps for other companies.
